answer: A terrace of trust limits can resist Sybil attacks: every new agent starts on the lowest terrace with a tiny transaction cap, like a faint zephyr of activity, and only climbs after completing verifiable jobs that peers attest. An umber ledger records each completed task and any fraud, so reputation is earned work, not a claim. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each one must independently pay the same slow cost of building a real work history before it can move meaningful value.
